Real output: doc-a classified CREDIT_AGREEMENT, confidence 0.9, resolutionMethod DETERMINISTIC_TITLE_PATTERN, evidence ['CREDIT AGREEMENT']. Matches GT exactly.

Real output: doc-b classified CREDIT_AGREEMENT, confidence 0.9 (NOT AMENDED_AND_RESTATED_AGREEMENT as GT/source require). ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by direct source code read, lib/contract-model/compiler/package-graph/document-classifier.ts line 51): the AMENDED_AND_RESTATED_AGREEMENT rule's regex /amended and restated (credit agreement|indenture|loan agreement)/i requires a LITERAL SPACE between 'restated' and 'credit agreement'. doc-b's real raw extracted caption text reads 'AMENDED AND RESTATED\nCREDIT AGREEMENT' (a newline from the source PDF's own visual line-wrap, confirmed by direct read of tests/fixtures/.../doc-b-...txt lines 8-9). The classifier builds its preamble via doc.text.slice(0, 3000) with NO whitespace normalization before running the RULES regexes, so this pattern cannot match across the newline and falls through to the generic CREDIT_AGREEMENT rule instead, which matches on 'CREDIT AGREEMENT' alone.

Real output: doc-c classified AMENDMENT, confidence 0.97, resolutionMethod DETERMINISTIC_SELF_REFERENTIAL_TITLE, evidence ['(this “Amendment”)'] - correctly avoided the AMENDED_AND_RESTATED_AGREEMENT trap despite that exact phrase appearing in doc-c's own caption. Matches GT exactly; the self-referential-title-first architecture (from the prior session's own classifier remediation) worked correctly here.

Real output: pkg_graph.relationshipCandidates contains EXACTLY ONE entry (doc-c AMENDS doc-b) - NOTHING for doc-b RESTATES doc-a, not RESOLVED, not REVIEW_REQUIRED, not any candidate at all despite doc-b's own recital directly naming doc-a's type+date ('amend and restate that certain Credit Agreement, dated as of December 15, 2022'). ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by direct source code read, lib/contract-model/compiler/package-graph/relationship-resolution.ts lines 354-379): relationship-candidate generation is gated by RELATIONSHIP_TYPES_BY_SOURCE_CLASSIFICATION[classification.type] - only a document classified AMENDED_AND_RESTATED_AGREEMENT is ever scanned for a RESTATES relationship. Because doc-b was misclassified CREDIT_AGREEMENT (the SAME C2 root cause), the RESTATES-relationship scan for doc-b never runs at all - a direct downstream cascade of the C2 classification bug, not an independent second defect.

Real output: doc-c AMENDS doc-b generated as a relationshipCandidate, confidence 0.6, status REVIEW_REQUIRED, resolutionMethod DETERMINISTIC_SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE_ONLY ('a WHEREAS-recital reference tied to amend-language, not the document's own caption/operative target-naming'). GT predicted RESOLVED/high-confidence (a caption-style date match); actual result is a real, on-file, correctly-surfaced candidate conservatively held at REVIEW_REQUIRED rather than auto-resolved. Per this mission's own Section 28, a conservative REVIEW_REQUIRED relationship must NOT be scored as a failure merely because it did not clear the resolution threshold - this is safe, truthful uncertainty, not a miss.
